ai.title: Add promptGeminiWithFallbacks and fix Vertex system message handling
ai.summary: New `backend/src/gemini-with-fallbacks.ts` standardizes Gemini API calls with automatic fallback to Vertex Gemini and then Claude/GPT-4o. `backend/src/gemini-vertex-api.ts` updated to reject inline system messages in favor of top-level `systemInstruction` via new `transformSystem` helper, fixing API errors. Call sites in `backend/src/find-files/` and `backend/src/planning.ts` refactored to use the new helper. Gemini 2 Flash timeout increased to 60s in `backend/src/gemini-api.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system asks an AI to look at files and decide what's relevant, it now uses a single smarter fallback path: it tries one AI service first, and if that fails or misbehaves, it quietly switches to a backup, then another, without interrupting the task. The instructions for how to talk to the Google Vertex AI service were rewritten so they match that service's exact format, preventing the errors that happened when the system sent instructions in the wrong shape. The result is that file-finding and planning steps behind the scenes are more likely to succeed on the first try and recover automatically instead of failing outright, and the Google Flash model now waits a bit longer (doubled tolerance) before giving up on slow replies.

ai.title: System prompt adds package install permission rule
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts adds rule 7 requiring permission before package installs, renumbering prior rule 7 to 8. Terminal command use cases now list Windows equivalents (mv/move, rm/del). New guidance instructs agent to ask permission for commands outside the three approved categories, displaying the command in triple-backtick tags.

eli5.text: The assistant now needs permission before installing new software packages, and it will show you the exact command it wants to run for anything else that falls outside building, testing, or moving/deleting files. When it asks, you'll see the command wrapped in triple backticks so you can review exactly what it's proposing. This affects anyone working with the assistant on a project, especially on larger ones where the assistant will err on the side of asking before making changes that touch package management.

ai.title: Fix file path attribute name and tighten command scope
ai.summary: Corrected `filePath` to `path` in file editing instructions within `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Clarified command execution rules to explicitly treat anything outside the project directory as read-only. This aligns system prompt guidance with actual tool schema and reinforces security boundaries for shell commands.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instructions now use clearer wording about how to name files when making edits and explicitly treat anything outside the project folder as read-only unless you give it permission to change it. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping that tightens existing safety rules; it does not add any new visible features or change what you can do today.
